bobDecision.summary: Staged upgrade to Node 20 recommended via Node 18 intermediate step
bobDecision.rationale: The staged approach reduces risk (7.9 vs 9.7) by allowing incremental validation. All identified issues are in test fixtures (tmp/dev2-fixtures/), not production code. The main codebase has no dependency blockers and uses modern TypeScript with proper module patterns. A staged upgrade through Node 18 allows testing Docker configurations and source patterns incrementally.
prioritizedRisks: Legacy Buffer constructor in test fixtures needs replacement with Buffer.from()
Mixed ESM/CommonJS patterns in test fixtures require module system alignment
module.parent usage needs refactoring to explicit entrypoint logic
process.binding() usage must be replaced with public APIs
Docker configurations in test fixtures need version updates
chosenSolutions: Phase 1: Update to Node 18 first, fixing Docker configs and source issues in test fixtures
Phase 2: Validate all tests pass on Node 18
Phase 3: Update to Node 20 after Node 18 validation
Replace legacy Buffer() with Buffer.from() in test fixtures
Standardize module system (prefer ESM) in test fixtures
Refactor module.parent to explicit entrypoint checks
Replace process.binding() with documented public APIs
tradeoffs: Staged approach requires two upgrade cycles but significantly reduces risk
Test fixture updates needed but production code is already compatible
More testing overhead but higher confidence in stability
